claim: In the authors' syllabification, morpheme-internal ei, eu, ai, au, ou, oi and ui are tautosyllabic diphthongs, while iu is not a permissible diphthong. Diphthongs are much rarer than short vowels, those beginning with /a/ are the most frequent, and word-initial /ui/ requires qualification because 7 of 17 /ui/ tokens occur initially where Mosel & Hovdhaugen report an initial [w]-glide realization.
formal_environment: VV within root; word-initial ui separately qualified
normalized_environment: DIPHTHONG = {ei,eu,ai,au,ou,oi,ui}; *iu as diphthong; #ui may surface with initial glide
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Special morpheme-boundary and idiolectal stress patterns can obey strict penultimate-mora footing instead; initial /ui/ may not be a phonetic diphthong because of [w].
publication_page: HTML edition; exact PDF pagination not exposed in accessible text

claim: Consonant-vowel combinations are mostly close to chance expectations, but /v/ before back vowels is the clearest exception: /vo/ is extremely rare and /vu/ is absent in the corpus. The authors call this a nearly categorical exclusion and relate it to Samoan /v/ being the historical reflex of *w.

source_forms.interpretation: nearly categorical exclusion of v before back vowels

normalized_environment: V strongly disfavored before BACK_VOWEL; vu unattested, vo near-gap
exceptions_or_counterexamples: /vo/ has two tokens, so this is explicitly near-categorical rather than categorical; overall consonant place has little predictive effect on following vowel identity.
publication_page: HTML edition; exact PDF pagination not exposed in accessible text

claim: Across syllables, Samoan exhibits gradient vowel assimilation: non-identical non-low vowels sharing front/back specification are under-represented relative to identical pairs. The pattern is static lexical co-occurrence rather than an alternation, and the expanded corpus supports weaker extensions to additional orders and even front+back non-low pairs.

source_forms.source_generalization: greater vowel similarity corresponds to stronger under-representation of non-identical pairs

normalized_environment: NONIDENTICAL NONLOW V-V pairs are gradiently disfavored, strongest when feature-similar
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Earlier Krupa generalization excluded /o-u/ and Samoan lacked the reported /e-i/ pattern; Alderete & Bradshaw find additional weaker effects, so no single categorical harmony rule captures all cells.
publication_page: HTML edition; exact PDF pagination not exposed in accessible text

claim: Homorganic consonant under-representation is strongly order-sensitive. In all roots, /m-p/ and /m-f/ have O/E values .52 and .77, while the reverse orders /p-m/ and /f-m/ have O/E 0.0. More generally, the restriction is weakened when a bilabial occurs initially and when a coronal sonorant occurs non-initially.

source_forms.positional_bias: bilabials preferred initially; non-labial/coronal sonorants preferred non-initially

normalized_environment: SAME_PLACE cooccurrence penalty conditioned by SEGMENT_ORDER + SYLLABLE_POSITION
scope: root corpus; identical consonants treated separately in analysis
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Not all same-place pairs are equally rare. The authors explicitly warn that reduced Samoan inventory makes it difficult to establish a simple labial-vs-coronal difference independent of order and manner.
publication_page: HTML edition; exact PDF pagination not exposed in accessible text

claim: Nasal co-occurrence is not captured by a blanket *ŋ...nasal ban. /ŋ...m/ is unattested and nasal-final /...ŋ/ combinations are generally depressed, but /ŋ...n/ has O/E 1.02 in the full root set and only .33 in disyllabic roots. Separately, /ŋ...ʔ/ and /ʔ...ŋ/ are under-represented (O/E .51 and .25 in all roots), plausibly reflecting historical homorganicity because Samoan /ʔ/ continues Proto-Polynesian *k.
normalized_environment: NG+NASAL restriction is pair/order/corpus-size sensitive; historical VELAR similarity may depress NG~GLOTTAL pairs
exceptions_or_counterexamples: /ŋ...n/ is not globally rare in the all-root corpus despite being low in disyllables; identical /ŋ...ŋ/ is over-represented. This directly blocks coding a categorical *ŋ...N constraint.
publication_page: HTML edition; exact PDF pagination not exposed in accessible text
